hypotheses.statement: For a finite exact call graph with declared host intrinsic effects, function effect summaries can be computed compositionally by monotone least-fixed-point closure without new ClayCode surface syntax.
evidence: 20,000 random cyclic call graphs, 0 reference mismatches; max 9 LFP rounds
hypotheses.falsifier: production parser/IR call graphs require non-monotone/context-sensitive semantics that make this summary unsound or prohibitively imprecise

hypotheses.statement: Required-capability propagation can remain static metadata while execution authority is supplied only by the runtime gateway, preserving expressibility != authority.
evidence: missing capability and textual-name forgery tests fail closed
hypotheses.falsifier: production FFI requires metadata to mint/attenuate authority implicitly to remain usable, with no safer explicit token path

hypotheses.statement: Source/contract identity, semantic program identity, lowered-artifact identity, and execution-trace identity should remain distinct and linked rather than collapsed.
evidence: format variant: different source+contract hash, same semantic+lowered hash; Harness H-WP-02 layered-identity result
hypotheses.falsifier: a single identity can preserve all required provenance, equivalence, cache, replay, and execution distinctions without false equality/inequality

counterhypotheses.statement: Per-function local annotations are sufficient; transitive closure across calls adds complexity without practical benefit.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: compile multi-layer APP-01/02/FRANK call graphs and compare false-negative/false-positive capability/effect diagnostics

counterhypotheses.statement: Capability requirement metadata can double as authority safely.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: forgery/revocation/delegation/replay matrix against opaque external tokens
